# Asterra AI (Home / index.php)

Single-page private-beta / early-access landing for **Asterra AI**, a secure AI-agent platform for ambitious, growing teams.

## Layout
Two-column CSS grid, collapsing to one column on mobile.
- **Left grid item:** neutral-950 content panel with navigation, hero, social proof, and footer.
- **Right grid item:** a native Elements Container that owns the image-panel sizing and contains the **Three.js Image Ripple** component.

The right Container uses:
- Full width
- 50vh height on mobile
- 100vh height from the lg breakpoint
- Full content width and height
- Stretch alignment
- Zero padding and margin
- Hidden overflow
- Neutral-950 fallback background

## Component notes
- **Three.js Image Ripple** is intentionally sizing-agnostic and fills its parent at 100% width and height.
- Its image is selected through the **Ripple Image** resource well in the Inspector.
- The native parent Container controls responsive height, width, spacing, and clipping.
- The shader responds to mouse, pointer, and touch movement.
- The source image remains visible if WebGL or the pinned Three.js CDN module cannot load.

## Notes / debt
- Navigation and footer/social links are plain text and not yet wired.
- The waitlist form has no SMTP or webhook delivery configured.
- Avatar overlap uses fixed-pixel translateX offsets (-12/-24/-36px) rather than theme tokens.

# Custom component instances render blank despite literal template output

## What was being attempted

Diagnose why the Pulsing Dot custom component does not render any visible output on the Asterra AI home page.

## Context

Custom component: Pulsing Dot. Page: Asterra AI home. The page correctly satisfies its PHP filename requirement.

## What was tried

1. Inspected the custom component definition and on-page instance.
2. Replaced dynamic Tailwind sizing with CSS custom-property sizing.
3. Replaced the template with fixed Tailwind utility classes.
4. Replaced the template with inline-style HTML.
5. Replaced the template with a literal inline SVG.
6. Replaced the template with a literal text span.
7. Checked the rendered page Markdown and node properties after each simplification.

## Expected behaviour

A custom component with a literal span, SVG, or plain text template should emit visible markup for its on-page instance.

## Actual behaviour

The Pulsing Dot instance remained absent from rendered page Markdown after progressively simplifying its template from a themed animated dot to a literal inline SVG and finally a plain text character. Its node stayed present in the page tree and had no hidden property. The instance was replaced with a native Text component as a fallback.

## Recommendations

1. Expose template compilation/rendering diagnostics for individual custom-component instances.
2. Provide an instance-level rendered HTML inspection tool or error state when a custom component emits no markup.
3. Investigate why custom component templates containing literal markup produce blank output in the page renderer.

## Resolution (2026-08-11)

Root cause confirmed by inspecting the real preview build (PHP preview server output):

1. **`{{id}}` interpolates to an empty string in preview/publish builds** for in-app custom components (docs claim `id` is a built-in, but it is not populated). CSS selectors like `.component-{{id}}` become `.component-` and match nothing, and `@keyframes name-{{id}}` produces broken names. Styles files that contained other `{{prop}}` interpolation (e.g. `{{dotSize}}`) were dropped from the build entirely.
2. **A template whose root element lacks an anchor** (after removing `component-{{id}}` from the root class) causes the whole instance to render blank — this was the original mystery in this report.

Working pattern (verified in preview for both Status Dot and Three.js Image Ripple):
- Scope all CSS with a **static component class** (e.g. `.status-dot`, `.three-ripple`) — no `{{…}}` in the Styles slot at all.
- Pass per-instance values as **inline CSS custom properties** (template interpolation of props works, e.g. `style="--dot-size: {{dotSize}}px"`) or as `data-*` attributes via Hooks.
- Build the root element in **Hooks with `rw.setRootElement`** when the root needs dynamic attributes.

Both components now render correctly in browser preview: pulsing dot visible in the badge, ripple filling its screen-height grid cell with WebGL active.

Leaders and operators at ambitious growing teams looking for practical, secure AI assistance across their work.

title: Writing Style
summary: Voice and tone guide — read before authoring any copy

## Voice & Tone
Confident, calm, and modern. Product marketing for a secure AI-agent platform built for ambitious teams. Aspirational but never hyperbolic.

## Sentence Rhythm
Short, declarative. Headlines make a clear promise ("Your company, amplified by AI."). Supporting copy stays focused on outcomes rather than technical detail.

## Vocabulary
Favours capable, grounded language: "secure", "agents", "understand", "automate", "moving". Avoids hype, jargon, and exclamation marks.

## Person & POV
Second person implied ("your company", "their work"). Brand referred to by name ("Asterra AI").

## Heading Style
Sentence case, declarative, occasionally paired with a single concise accent phrase.

## Caption & Label Style
Uppercase, wide letter-spacing, small size for eyebrows, badges, nav, footer, and social-proof labels. Button labels are title case ("Request Access").

## 2026-08-10 — Built Vela waitlist landing

Built the single-page Vela coming-soon landing from a user screenshot. Two-column split hero (black content panel + iridescent gradient image, AI-generated). Composed from primitives (no templates available): grid + flex + text + form. Set page to index.php (Form requires PHP). Seeded the design system (writing + visual) from this build. Known follow-ups: wire nav/footer links, configure Form delivery.

## 2026-08-10 — Refined Vela social proof

Generated and added four cohesive professional headshot resources to the Vela homepage social-proof row. Replaced the previous gradient placeholders with circular, dark-bordered portraits while preserving the compact staggered overlap and existing waitlist count.

## 2026-08-11 — Rebranded landing as Asterra AI

Rewrote the Vela landing page as **Asterra AI**, a secure AI-agent platform for ambitious teams. Updated navigation, private-beta message, hero copy, social proof, logo cloud, footer, browser metadata, site title, and writing guidance. Preserved the existing split-hero layout, portraits, and waitlist form.

## 2026-08-11

Repaired the **Pulsing Dot** custom component on [[pages/asterra-ai]]. Its size now uses an inline CSS custom property, allowing fractional theme spacing values to render correctly instead of depending on generated utility classes.

## 2026-08-11

Confirmed that the **Pulsing Dot** custom component renderer emitted no visible output even when reduced to literal HTML, SVG, and plain text. Replaced its sole on-page use with a native accent-coloured text dot to preserve the early-access badge; filed a field report for the renderer failure.

## 2026-08-11 — Pulsing Dot repair

Rebuilt the Pulsing Dot as a self-contained CSS core-and-ring animation. The pulse no longer depends on JavaScript and is intended to run in both the editor canvas and preview; reduced-motion preferences disable the expanding ring. Remaining debt: its accent colour is still a hardcoded hex pending a theme-backed component property.

## 2026-08-11 — Status Dot theme colour

Updated the Status Dot custom component to remove its Available/Unavailable segmented state. It now exposes one single-mode theme colour picker, applying the chosen theme background colour to both the solid core and pulse ring. Size and animation controls remain intact. Removed the resolved hardcoded-colour concern from [[pages/asterra-ai]] and regenerated [[concerns]].

## 2026-08-11 — Three.js ripple image settings

Built and placed the **Three.js Image Ripple** custom component in the right hero panel on [[pages/asterra-ai]]. It reacts to mouse, pointer, and touch movement, includes reduced-motion and static-image fallbacks, and exposes controls for the shader behavior. Replaced the original component dropzone with a **Ripple Image** resource well in the Inspector and preserved the existing holographic flower artwork. Recorded the pinned jsDelivr Three.js dependency in [[services]].

## 2026-08-11 — Standalone ripple sizing

Expanded the **Three.js Image Ripple** component with standalone sizing controls: responsive widths, alignment, fill/fixed/viewport/aspect-ratio height modes, and separate mobile/desktop values. Replaced the wrapped instance on [[pages/asterra-ai]] with an equivalent ripple directly inside the two-column hero Grid, then removed the obsolete right-side Background wrapper.

## 2026-08-11 — Ripple root sizing repair

Repaired the standalone **Three.js Image Ripple** sizing on [[pages/asterra-ai]]. Elements was stretching the custom-component wrapper to the Grid row while a shorter nested host contained the image, exposing a large white area beneath it in the editor. Moved the component classes, sizing, background, data attributes, and WebGL host onto the actual custom-component root via `rw.setRootElement()`, and removed the redundant nested host.

## 2026-08-11 — Native Container ripple layout

Replaced standalone custom-component sizing with a native Elements Container on [[pages/asterra-ai]]. The Container is the Grid’s right-hand item and owns responsive sizing (50vh mobile, 100vh at lg), clipping, and fallback background. The **Three.js Image Ripple** is now a simple 100% width/height child with no competing layout controls.

## 2026-08-11 — Ripple runtime repair

Restored the interactive runtime for the selected **Three.js Image Ripple** on [[pages/asterra-ai]]. The script had been explicitly skipping Elements edit mode, and an intermediate cleanup patch introduced invalid JavaScript. Removed the edit-mode guard, repaired the lifecycle/cleanup block, moved pointer tracking to `window` so the editor selection overlay does not intercept movement, limited activation to the image bounds, and rebuilt the live instance.

## 2026-08-11 — Ripple preview layer alignment

Fixed the Preview layer mismatch for the **Three.js Image Ripple** on [[pages/asterra-ai]]. Made the native Container a positioned frame, pinned the custom-component root to all four Container edges, and hid the fallback source image once WebGL reports ready so the canvas becomes the sole visible image layer.

## 2026-08-11 — Fixed Three.js Image Ripple layout break in preview

The Three.js Image Ripple custom component was breaking the page layout in preview. Root cause: its root element was styled `position: absolute; inset: 0`, so it sat outside normal flow and depended entirely on a positioned ancestor — fragile against the Core container's wrapper structure and able to overlay the page when anchoring escaped the intended cell. Fixed by making the root flow-based: `position: relative; width: 100%; height: 100%; flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 16rem` (inner image/canvas layers remain absolute within it). Verified against Core pack source that the parent container's content wrapper is `relative flex flex-col h-screen`, so the component now fills its grid cell exactly. Also fixed `@if(edit)` in the template referencing an undefined property — the hook now sets `edit: rw.project.mode === 'edit'` (previously only a `data-edit` attribute existed), and added a fallback to the `--color-neutral-950` background variable. User should re-run preview to confirm.

## 2026-08-11 — Root-caused and fixed custom component preview breakage

Follow-up to the ripple fix: preview was still broken. Inspected the actual preview build via the local PHP preview server and found `{{id}}` interpolates to an empty string in the Styles slot (and template) of custom components at build time, so every `.component-{{id}}` selector matched nothing — the Three.js Image Ripple rendered completely unstyled and its full-size source image blew out the page layout. Rewrote the ripple Styles scoped to the static `.three-ripple` class (no interpolation). Applied the same pattern to Status Dot (static `.status-dot` scoping, static keyframe name, size via inline `--dot-size` custom property, root element built in Hooks with `setRootElement`) — its CSS had been dropped from the build entirely and the dot was invisible in preview. Verified in a real browser: layout correct, WebGL ripple active (`is-ready`, canvas filling the 960×1080 cell), dot pulsing, no horizontal overflow. Field report closed with root cause and the working pattern.

## 2026-08-11 — Added Ambient strength slider; found inspector slider registration quirk

Added an "Ambient strength" slider to the Three.js Image Ripple (new `idleStrength` property → `data-idle-strength` → `uIdleStrength` shader uniform), and made ambient drift stronger/faster by default. In the process discovered that **slider property definitions with small fractional values are silently dropped from the component schema/inspector** — observed failures: `step: 0.002`, `step: 0.1`, `step: 0.001`, and `min: 0.5`; observed successes: `step: 1`, `step: 0.5` with `min >= 1`. The component's original Strength and Speed sliders had never actually appeared in the inspector because of this. Fix pattern: define sliders with integer-ish ranges (e.g. Strength 2–80 = thousandths, Ambient strength 1–50 = thousandths) and convert to the real value in Hooks when writing the `data-*` attribute. All six ripple properties now register and their values flow through to preview correctly.
